Advances: specled.prime, specled.next, specled.package

From the pre-ship critical review (consolidated 2026-07-25, CF1 + U9). Tier-1: the taught protocol sentence is FALSE as shipped and is replicated into adopter repos by the bootstrap skill.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION (consolidator): `mix spec.check --base definitely-not-a-real-ref --no-run-commands 2>&1 | tail -2` puts `** (Mix) --base ... does not resolve to a commit` AFTER the verdict line. Since a failing run always raises, and a terminal interleaves both streams, "The last line is the verdict" is false on every failure path in ordinary use, not just under 2>&1.

Current sentence (25 occurrences, must stay byte-identical everywhere):
"The last line is the verdict — `spec.check result=…`; nothing above it, including `validate status=…`, is the verdict."

Required properties of the replacement:
1. TRUE under merged stdout+stderr and in a terminal.
2. Anchors on the PREFIX (`spec.check result=`), not on line position.
3. Defines the absence case: no verdict line present => treat as failure (non-zero exit is the forgery-proof signal; exit codes verified non-zero on every failure path).
4. Still distinguishes the verdict from `validate status=…` (the original bug this epic exists to fix).
5. Byte-identical on every surface.

Proposed wording (refine if you can do better while keeping 1-5):
"The verdict is the last stdout line starting with `spec.check result=` — not `validate status=…`. A non-zero exit means failure even if no verdict line appears."

Surfaces to update (all 25 occurrences): lib/specled_ex/prime.ex, lib/specled_ex/next.ex, test/mix/tasks/spec_prime_task_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_next_task_test.exs, .spec/specs/prime.spec.md, .spec/specs/next.spec.md, .spec/AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/specled.md, docs/adoption.md (x3), docs/concepts.md, docs/coverage.md, skills/spec-led-bootstrap/SKILL.md (x3), references/adoption-phases.md (x3), references/detection-matrix.md, references/configurable-levers.md (x2).

ALSO (U9, same files): docs/coverage.md:47 appends the sentence to a paragraph about `mix spec.cover.test` exit codes, but spec.cover.test never emits a verdict line (print_verdict exists only in spec.check.ex/spec.validate.ex) — relocate it to a real spec.check passage in that file or drop that occurrence. Same for the mid-list occurrence in configurable-levers.md if it lands on an unrelated passage.

Also consider hoisting the sentence to ONE shared constant in lib/ referenced by prime.ex, next.ex and both test files (CF3) — it contains U+2014 and U+2026, so retyped copies can differ invisibly.

OUT OF SCOPE: the tier=usage grammar change, tagged_tests attribution fixes, drain-helper channel work, fixture severity mix (all batched to the fast-follow). No lib/ behavior change beyond the sentence constant.

NOTE (out-of-repo handoff): .claude/rules/specled.md is agent-rules-sync-managed. The in-repo edit is correct, but the vault source at ~/dev/mz/agentic-dotfiles/llms/workflows/agent-rules/rules/specled.md needs the identical reword or the next sync reverts it. Record this in the completion record; the orchestrator applies it.

Verification: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check (bare). Plus: prove by execution that the new sentence is true on a failure path (run spec.check with a bad --base under 2>&1 and confirm the sentence text accurately describes what a reader sees).

Reasoning: The Gap's mechanism is real — I traced it without re-running anything: next.ex:6 holds `@verdict_read_protocol`, next.ex:8 exposes it, next.ex:320 appends `verdict_read_protocol()` to the suggestions and prime.ex:82 delegates to `Next.verdict_read_protocol()`, while spec_prime_task_test.exs:23 and spec_next_task_test.exs:24 bind `@verdict_protocol SpecLedEx.Next.verdict_read_protocol()` and the only three assertions (prime:54, prime:154, next:63) are `contains?(output, @verdict_protocol)`, so both sides of every comparison are the same constant and the mutation claim holds. But the FAIL rests on a framing the base tree falsifies: `git show f338abb:lib/specled_ex/prime.ex` line 82 and `git show f338abb:test/mix/tasks/spec_prime_task_test.exs` line 23 both carried the OLD, FALSE sentence as matching independent literals with the suite green, so the removed tripwire never guarded "a wrong sentence shipping" — it guarded lib↔test divergence, which is precisely the U+2014/U+2026 drift hazard CF3 named and which the hoist now eliminates by construction rather than by test. Every one of the ticket's five required properties was proven TRUE by execution by the verifier itself, and property 5 (byte-identical) is now strictly stronger than at base: I independently confirmed all 16 single-line copies collapse to one uniq class and the `>-`-folded next.spec.md:69-72 copy resolves to the same string. That combination is Note-plus-fast-follow shaped, not FAIL, and the seam was authored by the ticket's own instruction rather than by the implementer.

Findings by axis:

1. Mutation claim — STRUCTURALLY SOUND. Traced above. The assertion genuinely reads the same compile-time constant the production output is built from; a mutated constant body would leave all three assertions green. Verifier is correct on the mechanism.

2. Regression, not pre-existing — CORRECT, but narrower than claimed. At f338abb there were FOUR independent literals (prime.ex:82, next.ex:318, spec_prime_task_test.exs:23, spec_next_task_test.exs:24) yielding two genuine lib↔test cross-checks. Those are now one constant with two derived references. So "this diff removed the tripwire" is factually right. What it did NOT remove is any guard against falsity — the base tree is the counterexample, since the false sentence sat in all four literals and passed. The Gap should have said "a unilateral edit to the shared constant is now silent," not "removes the only mechanical tripwire for that exact failure mode."

3. Ticket authorship — CONFIRMED, and it changes the routing. The ticket's own text reads "Also consider hoisting the sentence to ONE shared constant in lib/ referenced by prime.ex, next.ex and both test files (CF3)". It names both test files as referencing consumers. The implementer built exactly that. Grading the implementer down for the resulting tautology is grading them for compliance. The ticket should have said: "...referenced by prime.ex and next.ex; keep ONE golden test asserting the constant against a literal so the text cannot change silently, and have the task tests reference the constant." That sentence is what was missing, and it is a ticket-authoring defect.

4. Remediation — (a) IS a genuine tripwire, not a relocated duplicate: a single `assert SpecLedEx.Next.verdict_read_protocol() == "<literal>"` forces any future wording change to be a deliberate two-place edit, which is the standard golden-test shape. It restores deliberateness, not truth, and that is the right scope. (b) IS SCOPE EXPANSION and should be dropped from this ticket. I diffed the `spec-verification` block of package.spec.md between f338abb and HEAD — byte-IDENTICAL. The existence-only `kind: source_file` entries for `specled.package.adoption_guide` (package.spec.md:126-128) and `concepts_guide` (:129-132) are untouched by this diff; the seam is pre-existing and belongs to the fast-follow. Adding an `execute: true` grep over 14 markdown surfaces would also newly bind the doc corpus into the gate, well past the ticket's "No lib/ behavior change beyond the sentence constant." Simpler sufficient fix: (a) alone.

5. Counts — VERIFIER IS RIGHT ON BOTH, re-derived independently. Old: `git grep -n "is the verdict" f338abb` returns 24 matching lines; exactly two are continuation lines of a two-line sentence (.claude/rules/specled.md:33 and .spec/specs/prime.spec.md:63), giving 22 distinct instances. The ticket's "25" and the implementer's "25 old sites handled" are both wrong. New: grepping the fold-surviving fragment "last stdout line starting with" returns 17 — 16 single-line plus the folded .spec/specs/next.spec.md:69-72 copy. The implementer's "16 live" is wrong by exactly that folded copy. Arithmetic reconciles: 22 − 2 dropped (docs/coverage.md, configurable-levers.md:94) − 3 collapsed (prime.ex, both test literals) = 17.

6. Three-falsehoods routing — CORRECT AS ROUTED, and the verifier was if anything too hard on itself. I read all three hunks in `git diff f338abb..HEAD -- skills/`. In every case the diff replaced ONLY the appended protocol sentence and the false clause is pre-existing prose that merely shares the line: SKILL.md's changed text is "not its version string). <sentence>" with the `detector_unavailable`/`umbrella_unsupported` probe instruction on the preceding context lines; adoption-phases.md:110's changed text is "still warning-level, so it reports without hard-failing). <sentence>"; adoption-phases.md:30's is "silent. <sentence>". That is line collision, not authorship. Fast-follow (specled_-xde, specled_-j3k) is the right home.

Scope check (independent): `git diff --name-only f338abb..HEAD` = 17 files, none matching the Out of Scope list — no tier=usage grammar change, no tagged_tests attribution work, no drain-helper channel change, no fixture severity edits. lib/ delta is exactly the constant, its accessor, one call site in next.ex and one delegation in prime.ex. .spec/state.json is gitignored so its absence from the diff is correct, and .spec/realization_hashes.json is tracked and unchanged, consistent with `SpecLedEx.Next.run/3`'s implementation-tier binding surviving its 6→10 line shift. One note the verifier did not raise: the diff adds a prose paragraph to .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md, a subject NOT in this ticket's Advances list — harmless (narrative only, no requirement or verification change) but it should be named in the completion record rather than left implicit.

Bounce reason: Re-issue the verdict with the Gap corrected, and do not re-route this to the implementer. Specifically: (1) Downgrade the Gap to a Note, or keep it as a Gap only if you can name a hazard the base tree did not already have — the base tree's four matching FALSE literals with a green suite is the disproof of "removes the only mechanical tripwire for that exact failure mode," and byte-identity across lib and both test files is now guaranteed by construction where at base it was only asserted. (2) State explicitly that the seam is TICKET-AUTHORED: the ticket instructed the hoist "referenced by prime.ex, next.ex and both test files," so the implementer complied; the missing clause was a golden test, which the ticket never asked for. Route the fix as a ticket-authoring correction and a small fast-follow, not an implementer bounce. (3) Drop remediation (b) from this ticket. The package.spec.md `spec-verification` block is byte-identical between f338abb and HEAD, so the existence-only `adoption_guide`/`concepts_guide` seam is pre-existing and out of scope here; carry it to the same fast-follow that holds specled_-xde/specled_-j3k. (4) Keep remediation (a) as the fast-follow's content — one `assert SpecLedEx.Next.verdict_read_protocol() == "<literal>"` golden test — and say plainly it restores deliberateness, not truth. (5) Correct the two count claims in the record: 22 old instances (not the ticket's or the implementer's 25) and 17 live (not 16); you had both right, so carry them forward into the corrected verdict so the completion record stops repeating 25/16.
